sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 covers the northern edge of South River beside the South River, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the lower left. The upper third is taken by the South River Brick Co., manufacturers of brick and lumber dealers, with a long kiln shed, dryers, brick machines, storage sheds, an office and lumber yards with dashed outlines marking stacked lumber, and a siding to the Raritan River Railroad at the upper left. Reid runs diagonally down the page from the brickworks to Prospect at the bottom, with a second Reid line running across the top of the residential blocks towards George, which runs down the right edge. Stephen and Thomas cross the lower part between Reid and George. The blocks, numbered 45, 46, 69 and 70, are laid out in long narrow house lots carrying one- and two-storey frame dwellings with outbuildings; larger buildings are the United Underwear Co. works beside Reid, a handkerchief factory, and a dress factory with power and lights on Thomas and Stephen. Maple Avenue crosses the lower left on a different alignment, with blocks numbered 9 beyond it. A compass rose stands at the left. Water pipes of four and six inches run in Reid, Stephen, George and Thomas. The edges meet sheets 3, 4 and 9.
notes: Reid, Stephen, George, Thomas and Maple are Reid Street, Stephen Street, George Street, Thomas Street and Maple Street in OpenStreetMap.
Reid Street / Thomas Street was left out: the detector placed it off the sheet. The map is drawn with Reid becoming Prospect at the lower left.
map, 50 ft, north to the lower left. South River Brick Co. at top; Reid, Stephen, George, Thomas, Maple Av, Prospect.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 covers the commercial centre of South River, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that Main Street runs across the page. Main Street is the principal business street, with continuous rows of brick and frame stores and offices on both sides, among them the Capitol Theatre, the Star Theatre, a National Bank building, Borough Hall and the fire department at the upper left, and hotel and factory buildings near the South River at the upper right. George runs along the top of the sheet, with Thomas, Stephen and Reid crossing it towards Main. South of Main the blocks, numbered 127, 130, 131, 132A, 132B, 133, 134A, 134B and 135, are laid out between Washington, Obert, Marks Place, Ferry and Water; Eberwein and Klauser Lane run off Ferry and Water at the right. Along the lower edge Jackson crosses on a diagonal, meeting Ferry at White Head Avenue, with Holmes Avenue and Radcliffe near the lower left. Dense commercial blocks with stores, a telephone exchange, a printing works, garages and mills occupy the middle of the sheet, while the lower left is mostly open lots with scattered dwellings and outbuildings. Water pipes run in all the main streets. The sheet adjoins sheets 2, 4, 5 and 8, and a compass rose stands at the lower right.
notes: Klauser Lane is Klausers Lane and White Head Avenue is Whitehead Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
map, 50 ft. Downtown: Main St, Washington, Ferry, Jackson, Obert, Radcliffe, Water, White Head Av.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 covers a residential district in the north-west of South River, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that the streets run across and down the page. Thomas runs along the top, Leland Avenue, Clinton and Bright cross the middle, and John closes the sheet near the bottom. Zeigert runs down the left side and George down the middle, with Main along the right edge, where a garage and the post office stand at the upper right. The blocks, numbered 47 and 64 to 68, are laid out in narrow house lots; most lots carry one- and two-storey frame dwellings with small outbuildings, while large areas, especially the lower left and the south end of the blocks, are open. The principal building is South River High School No. 1, a brick fireproof school with a long wing, in block 67 beside George near the top. Frontage along George and Main below Bright is built up with detached dwellings and a few larger frame buildings. A compass rose stands at the left, and a short street lettered Daily is drawn at the bottom left. Water pipes run in the main streets. The sheet adjoins sheets 2, 3, 5 and 12.
notes: Leland Avenue, Clinton, Bright, John and Zeigert are Leland Avenue, Clinton Street, Bright Street, John Street and Zeigert Street in OpenStreetMap.
Clinton is lettered with (Av) in brackets.
map, 50 ft. Thomas, Leland Av, Clinton (Av), Bright, John, Zeigert, George, Main; High School No. 1.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 covers the western edge of the business district of South River, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that Main Street runs down the left edge. Along Main, at the top left, stand a row of brick stores, the Public Library and other commercial buildings with party walls marked; further down the east frontage is mixed frame dwellings and a church. Washington Street runs down the middle of the sheet, crossed by Gordon and Radcliffe, with blocks numbered 121, 126, 128 and 129 laid out on either side in narrow lots carrying one- and two-storey frame dwellings, a German Presbyterian church, a Methodist church, a dress factory and an embroidery works. Jackson crosses the lower right on a diagonal, with Wilson Avenue leaving it to the south-east; a second street lettered Jackson runs at the right edge. East of Washington the blocks follow the angle of Jackson in long lots, many only partly built. The lower left is largely open land with a few dwellings, and a compass rose and the scale bar stand at the right and bottom. The sheet adjoins sheets 3, 4, 12, 13, 14 and 15, and a dashed street lettered Thomas runs in at the top left.
notes: Street names carry no suffix on the sheet except Wilson Avenue; in OpenStreetMap they are Main Street, Washington Street, Gordon Street, Radcliffe Street, Jackson Street and Wilson Avenue.
map, 50 ft. Main, Washington, Gordon, Radcliffe, Jackson, Wilson Av.

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 covers the south-western part of South River between the Causeway and Whitehead Avenue, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that the streets run diagonally across the page, with a compass rose at the top. Water Street crosses the upper half and Whitehead Avenue the middle; Jackson runs down the left edge, Martin Avenue and Elizabeth Street run down the centre, and Lee, lettered with Charles in brackets, runs down the right with Russell Avenue beyond. Milton Avenue crosses the right side below Water, and Holmes Avenue and Obert cross the lower left. Charles, Willet Lane and Lincoln run diagonally across the lower centre. The blocks, numbered 141 to 146 and 151 to 155, are laid out in narrow house lots, most of them carrying one- and two-storey frame dwellings. The principal works are the Middlesex Embroidery Works and other embroidery factories, the R. & P. Wash Suit Co., and an automobile repair shop near the river. Churches and institutions include St. Mary's Polish Catholic Church with its rectory, St. Mary's Parochial School, Trinity Episcopal Church and a synagogue. The upper left shows the South River and its marsh, and salt meadows are lettered across the top. A ten-inch water pipe runs in Whitehead Avenue. The sheet adjoins sheets 3, 5, 7, 12, 13, 15 and 27.
notes: Lee is lettered with (Charles) in brackets, and a second street lettered Charles runs diagonally at the lower right.
Martin Avenue is not an OpenStreetMap street name; Russell Avenue and Willet Lane are Russel Avenue and Willett Lane in OpenStreetMap.
Detector: 11 points; Milton Avenue and Russel Avenue are not drawn on the modern line (Milton / Russel was left out as control).
map, 50 ft. Water, Whitehead Av, Elizabeth, Milton Av, Charles, Causeway; Russell Av left out (residuals).

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 covers a thinly built district on the north-western edge of South River, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north pointing down and slightly to the right. William Street runs down the right side and Cole Street down the centre, crossed by Burton Avenue in the upper middle and Florence Avenue in the lower left; June and Belmont Avenue run in from the right near the bottom, Eastern crosses William Street at the right, and Northern runs down the left edge and curves across the lower left. Philip is a street drawn at the upper left. Most of the sheet is vacant block land, numbered 21 to 24, 31 to 34, 38 and 8, laid out in lots but largely undeveloped; the built lots hold a few frame dwellings and outbuildings along Burton Avenue, Cole and William Street, with several larger buildings near the right edge. At the top the J. & G. Barnes Co. manufactured gas works, a brick building with a holder, stands beside two diagonal railroad tracks and a coal yard running across the upper part of the sheet. A bottling and ice works stands on Cole Street. A compass rose is at the upper right and the scale bar at the bottom. The sheet adjoins sheets 4, 6 and 8 to 12.
notes: Northern is today's Northern Street, and Burton Avenue, Cole, William, Eastern, Florence Avenue, June and Belmont Avenue are Burton Avenue, Cole Street, William Street, Eastern Street, Florence Avenue, June Street and Belmont Avenue.
Philip has no match in the OpenStreetMap extract.
William Street junctions with Burton Avenue and Eastern Street were left out as control: they sat 4 to 5 m off the fit from the other points.
map, 50 ft, north up. Burton Av, Cole, William, Florence Av, Northern, Philip; gas works at top. William/Burton and William/Eastern excluded (4-5 m off).

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 covers the older residential and light-industrial district of South River north-west of the Prospect Street crossing, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north up. Prospect runs down the page from the upper left to the foot of the sheet, where it turns east along the bottom edge. June and Florence Avenue cross it as two long parallel streets running from the upper right to the lower left, with Cole and Northern branching off Florence Avenue and Woodlawn Avenue curving across the upper left corner. In the right half Chestnut runs down the page from June to Prospect, crossed by Henry and Nelson, and William forms the right-hand boundary. Blocks 35 to 41D are mostly small frame dwellings with outbuildings, with brick and tile buildings in the older parts. Notable buildings include the Hungarian R.C. Church on Chestnut and William, the South River Laundry at the foot of Chestnut, a line of auto repair and concrete block buildings on June, and tile works at the top near Cole. Hydrants and four- to eight-inch water pipes are marked in most streets, and street widths of 37 to 52 feet are lettered. A fire alarm box stands at the Prospect and June crossing. Sheet 7 adjoins at the top, sheet 9 at the right and sheet 40 is named below.
notes: Prospect is East Prospect Street in OpenStreetMap; Woodlawn, Florence, Rose, Nelson, Chestnut, Henry, William and Cole carry the same names with modern suffixes (Cole Street, June Street, Chestnut Street and so on).
Northern and Leroy are lettered without a suffix.
Street names were read from the sheet overview at street-label size, not from full-resolution crops; medium confidence for small lettering.
map, 50 ft, north up. Woodlawn Av, Florence Av, Cole, June, Prospect, Rose, Nelson, Chestnut, Henry, William, Belmont Av, Leroy.

sheet-9.description: Sheet 9 covers the eastern edge of the built-up part of South River, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north up. William runs down the left edge of the sheet and is crossed by Belmont Avenue at the top, Leroy, Henry and, at the foot, Prospect. Maple (Av.) runs down the page through the middle, with a short street lettered Watts beside it, and Reid runs off to the lower right from the Prospect end. The blocks between William and Maple, numbered 42, 44 and 45, hold small frame dwellings with outbuildings, a bakery with ovens and a sales room on Leroy, a barber shop, embroidery works and a factory, an embroidery factory on Maple, a dress factory with power, light and steam heat on Henry, and Public School No. 3 near the foot. The upper right is a large triangular block, 43, mostly vacant, cut diagonally by a railroad siding lettered R.R.R. (Siding), at the end of which stand the South River Brick Co. buildings and a lime house. East of Maple the ground is largely open, with a dilapidated ice house, a few isolated buildings in block 46 and a compass rose, the margin lettered No Exposure at the top. Water pipes and hydrants are marked in most streets. Sheet 8 adjoins on the left and sheet 7 above.
notes: Prospect is East Prospect Street in OpenStreetMap; William, Belmont, Leroy, Henry and Reid keep their names with modern suffixes. Maple and Watts have no equivalent in the OpenStreetMap extract.
Placed from four junctions along William only, so this is a helmert with scale and rotation weakly constrained.
Street names were read from the sheet overview at street-label size, not from full-resolution crops; medium confidence for small lettering.
map, 50 ft, north up. William, Belmont Av, Leroy, Henry, Maple, Prospect, Watts; control only along William (helmert).

sheet-10.description: Sheet 10 covers a residential district on the western edge of South River, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned on the page so that north points to the left. Wilcox Avenue runs down the page near the left side and Devoe Avenue down the right side; between them the cross streets Darrow, Colfax (also lettered Glen), Beryl and Albourne run across the sheet, with Park Avenue just touching the top edge. Blocks 228 to 234 are laid out in narrow numbered house lots, most of them still vacant in 1930. The built lots carry small one- and two-storey frame dwellings with outbuildings, concentrated on Beryl and Albourne between Wilcox and Devoe and along Devoe Avenue; a few brick or tile buildings stand on the Darrow frontage west of Wilcox. The lower part of the sheet is crossed diagonally by the Old Bridge-New Brunswick Turnpike, along which the borough limit between South River and East Brunswick Township runs; south of the turnpike the land is lettered East Brunswick Township, with a short unnamed street drawn and a few dwellings on block 48. A six-inch water pipe and a hydrant are marked on the turnpike, and water pipes run in Darrow, Colfax, Beryl, Albourne and Wilcox. Large areas of the upper left are undeveloped block interiors. Neighbouring sheets 11, 21 and 22 adjoin along the top and right edges.
notes: Wilcox Avenue, Darrow, Colfax, Beryl and Albourne keep their names (Darrow Street, Colfax Street, Beryl Street, Albourne Street); Devoe Avenue is Devoe Street; the Old Bridge-New Brunswick Turnpike is Old Bridge Turnpike.
Colfax is lettered with Glen in brackets as an alternative name.
A street south of the turnpike is lettered Not Named.
map, 50 ft, north to the left. Wilcox Av to Devoe Av, Darrow, Colfax (Glen), Beryl, Albourne; Old Bridge-New Brunswick Tpke and East Brunswick line at bottom. Pilot sheet (ink 100).

sheet-11.description: Sheet 11 covers the western part of the town between Main Street and Darrow Street. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned on the page so that north points to the left, as on sheet 10. Wilcox Avenue runs down the page left of centre and Devoe Avenue (Av.) near the right edge. Cross streets lettered Garwood, Ferris, Edgewood, Birchwood Pl. and Darrow run across the sheet, with Park Av. and a short Wilcox Pl. on the right. Main Street crosses the upper part diagonally from the upper left to the right and Pottery Lane and Grove branch from it. W. George runs diagonally across the middle in two stretches and George appears at the top. The left side, blocks 236 to 238 (sheet 12 beyond), is open land with a single dwelling. The centre block 61 and 60B carry the larger buildings: a tile and brick works, an embroidery factory, a vacated and dilapidated concrete block building and a garage with auto and trucks, with a repair shop beside it. The blocks 59 and 60A beside Park Av. and Devoe are small frame dwellings. Water pipes of four to ten inches and several hydrants are marked, and street widths of 50 feet are lettered on most streets. Sheets 10 below, 12 and 22 adjoin.
notes: Devoe is Devoe Street today; W. George is West George Street; Birchwood Pl. is Birchwood Place; Darrow is Darrow Street.
Devoe Street junctions sat 5 to 8 m from the fit and were left out of the control; Park Avenue and West George Street was detected 80 ft from its seed and excluded.
Street names were read from the sheet overview at street-label size, not from full-resolution crops; medium confidence for small lettering.
map, 50 ft, north to the left. Wilcox Av, Garwood, Ferris, Edgewood, Birchwood Pl, Park Av, W. George; Devoe junctions 5-8 m off, left out.

sheet-12.description: Sheet 12 covers the district north-east of Wilcox Avenue between Daily Street and Main Street. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 30 degrees, north pointing up and to the left. George runs down the middle of the sheet in a long bend from the top to the foot, with Garwood on its west side, parallel to it, and Daily at the left. Virginia crosses the sheet twice, once on the left between Daily and Garwood and again on the right between George and Main. John is at the top right and Main Street runs down the right edge, where Jackson joins it. Ferris and Newell run along the lower left, and Wilcox Av. closes the foot of the sheet. Blocks 239 to 240 and 237 to 238 at the left are open land with a handful of dwellings; the blocks along George and Garwood (39, 62 and 63) are built with small frame houses and outbuildings, a tile building and some brick buildings, with a greenhouse on Main. Hydrants and water pipes of four to ten inches are marked, and street widths of 40 to 60 feet are lettered. A fire alarm box stands on Main at Jackson. Sheet 11 adjoins on the left and sheet 13 below on the right.
notes: Names match today's streets with suffixes (Daily Street, Virginia Street, Garwood Street, George Street, John Street, Main Street, Jackson Street, Ferris Street, Newell Street, Wilcox Avenue).
Junctions on Main Street and Garwood Street carry residuals of 3 to 5 m in the fit; John Street and Main Street was excluded.
Street names were read from the sheet overview at street-label size, not from full-resolution crops; medium confidence for small lettering.
map, 50 ft, turned about -30. Daily, Virginia, Garwood, George, John, Main, Jackson, Ferris, Newell, Wilcox Av.

sheet-13-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 13 is the main map, an L-shaped area in the west-central part of South River drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points up and to the left. Its upper half follows Jackson Street, which runs diagonally across the sheet from Main Street at the left edge to Washington Street, which ends against it near the top; beyond Washington the lots run on to Wilson Avenue, with Grochowiak Street leaving Wilson Avenue at the upper right. The south side of Jackson Street is divided into long, narrow numbered house lots carrying one- and two-storey frame dwellings with small outbuildings; the north side, block 126, is largely open, with one large dwelling. A narrow strip down the left side of the sheet shows the east frontage of Main Street from Jackson Street south to Wilcox Avenue, a row of frame dwellings on deep lots, with the Tabernacle Baptist Church and a fire alarm box near the Jackson Street corner. John Street leaves Main Street at the upper left. A ten-inch water pipe runs in Main Street and an eight-inch pipe in Jackson Street. A heavy line separates this part from part 2, the athletic field and the blocks between Fairview and Claremont Avenues, which occupy the lower right of the sheet. Neighbouring sheets 5, 12, 14, 23, 25 and 26 are referred to around the edges.
notes: The east side of Main Street is drawn; its west side belongs to sheet 12.
Washington Street ends at Jackson Street (T junction).

map, 50 ft, two parts split by a heavy line. Part 1 (L-shape): Jackson St from Main to Washington and Wilson Av, plus the east frontage of Main St down to Wilcox Av; few junctions, 3 hand-picked. Part 2 (lower right, own north arrow): athletic field, David to James St, Fairview to Claremont Av.

sheet-13-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 13 occupies the lower right of the sheet, below a heavy dividing line, and has its own north arrow; it is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points up and to the left. It covers the western residential district around the athletic field: at the top the open athletic field with a small frame dressing-room building, and below it David Street crossing the part, with James Street along the bottom edge. Fairview Avenue runs down the left side of the part, beside the dividing line, and Arlington, Lexington and Claremont Avenues run between David and James Streets. The blocks, numbered 96 to 103 and 242, are laid out in narrow house lots, many still vacant; the built lots carry one- and two-storey frame dwellings, several noted as drawn from plans, with small outbuildings. Four-inch and six-inch water pipes are marked in David Street and the avenues, with hydrants at the corners. The scale bar is drawn at the lower right. Neighbouring sheets 25 and 26 are referred to at the left and bottom edges.
notes: Several dwellings on David Street are marked as drawn from plans (not yet built when surveyed).

map, 50 ft, two parts split by a heavy line. Part 1 (L-shape): Jackson St from Main to Washington and Wilson Av, plus the east frontage of Main St down to Wilcox Av; few junctions, 3 hand-picked. Part 2 (lower right, own north arrow): athletic field, David to James St, Fairview to Claremont Av.

sheet-14.description: Sheet 14 covers the area between Wilson Avenue and Willet Avenue, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north up. Wilson Av. runs down the left side of the sheet and Raritan Av. down the middle right, with Willet Av. along the right edge. Jackson is lettered at the top, with Grochowiak, Sontag, Joseph and Franklin running across the sheet; Charles and a short Willet Lane are at the top right and Miller at the right edge near the bottom. The top block, number 250, is largely open land with a dwelling, a concrete block building and a Polish club and hall. Blocks 252, 253 and 255 along Sontag and Joseph are built with small frame dwellings and a few brick buildings. East of Raritan Av., block 136 holds an auto storage building and a large factory with lights and power electric, an embroidery factory, a tile building and dwellings, and across the foot at the right is a large vacant factory building in block 16. The left margin carries a note lettered No Exposures beside block 121. Water pipes and hydrants are marked in the streets, and widths of 40 to 100 feet are lettered. Sheet 13 adjoins on the left, 15 on the right and 5 above.
notes: Willet Avenue is Willett Avenue and Willet Lane is Willett Lane in OpenStreetMap; the other streets keep their names with modern suffixes.
Street names were read from the sheet overview at street-label size, not from full-resolution crops; medium confidence for small lettering.
map, 50 ft. Jackson, Grochowiak, Sontag, Joseph, Franklin, Wilson Av, Raritan Av, Willet Av, Charles, Miller.

sheet-15.description: Sheet 15 covers the north-eastern part of the town, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north up. Willet Av. runs down the left edge, with Stanton and Lincoln as parallel streets farther right and Anderson beyond them. Charles crosses the sheet at about a third of the height and Miller closes it at the foot, with a short Willet Lane (Pl.) above Charles. At the top left Jackson and Obert meet and run off the sheet towards the upper left, and in the lower right Division and Brook run diagonally. The centre block 148 holds Willet School No. 2, a large pink brick building, and a few small dwellings and an embroidery shop. The blocks west of Stanton, number 138, include the Kosciusko Bros. Embroidery Co. and rows of frame dwellings. East of Lincoln, block 149, are dwellings and an embroidery factory and an embroidery shop. In the right part the Lunepp Lace and Embroidery Co., makers of lace and underwear, occupies a large triangular block between Anderson and Division, with an underwear factory and an embroidery factory. Whitehead Av. appears at the upper right. Hydrants and water pipes are marked in all streets. Sheets 14, 16 and 17 adjoin.
notes: Willet Avenue is Willett Avenue and Willet Lane is Willett Lane in OpenStreetMap; the other streets keep their names with modern suffixes.
Street names were read from the sheet overview at street-label size, not from full-resolution crops; medium confidence for small lettering.
map, 50 ft. Willet Av, Stanton, Lincoln, Anderson, Charles, Miller, Jackson, Obert, Division, Brook, Whitehead Av.

sheet-16.description: Sheet 16 covers the western edge of the built-up town of South River, between Raritan Avenue on the west and Northside Avenue and Brook Street on the northeast. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north near the top. The upper half shows two blocks of dwellings, mostly frame with outbuildings, laid out around Miller Street, Stanton Street and Lincoln Street; the lots are numbered and a fire alarm box stands at the corner of Brook and Lincoln. Division Street runs east to west across the middle and then bends to the northeast as a diagonal street lined with narrow, deep dwelling lots down to Northside Avenue, where a row of larger houses and an embroidery works face the street. The lower left of the sheet is given to the Clayton Lumber Co., with a large lumber shed, cement storage, a wood working and sanding shop, window sill storage and a long run of lumber sheds curving along the railroad. Two tracks of the railroad cross the sheet from lower left to upper right and cut through Willet Avenue and the lumber yard; the line is labelled with Clayton Lumber Co. spur tracks. A cemetery is lettered at the lower left, and the corner of an adjoining block with Magiera and Union Avenue appears at the lower right. Four-inch and six-inch water pipes are marked in the streets, and the sheet edges refer to sheets 14, 15, 17 and 18.
notes: Willet Av. is today's Willett Avenue; Magiera is today's Mageira Street; Division, Miller, Stanton, Lincoln and Brook keep their names.
The railroad on this sheet is the Raritan River Railroad (modern Sayreville Running Track in OpenStreetMap).
Fit rests on six street junctions; the two Division Street junctions near Willett and Stanton carry residuals of about 5 to 6 m, so the horizontal stretch of Division may differ from its modern line.
map, 50 ft. Raritan River R.R. yard and Clayton Lumber Co.; Willet Av, Miller, Stanton, Division, Lincoln, Raritan Av. Division junctions 4.8-6 m off (kept, few points).

sheet-17.description: Sheet 17 shows the residential and small industrial area east of South River's centre, bounded on the north by Division Street and on the east by Whitehead Avenue. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and is turned so that north points toward the upper right, as the compass at the right shows, which makes Whitehead Avenue run nearly down the page. The top strip shows two rows of dwellings and outbuildings facing Division Street and Northside Avenue, with embroidery works among them. At the upper right, Russell Avenue and Herman Avenue cross Milton Avenue and Water, and the South River Cigar Co. (a branch of the General Cigar Co. Inc.) occupies a large pink-coloured brick mill along Water Street, with the South River Romper Co. beside it. The middle of the sheet is crossed by the Raritan River R. R., with a coal trestle, the A. W. Bisset coal, wood and ice yard with an ice house and ice machines, and Brown, Rose & Co. feed warehouse near Yates Avenue. Below the railroad lie blocks of frame dwellings along Jeffrie Avenue and Spring Street, with several embroidery works, a Russian chapel and a vacant tile building. Magiera runs along the foot of the sheet. Water pipes of four, six and ten inches are marked in the streets, and neighbouring sheets 6, 15, 16, 18, 19 and 20 are cited at the edges.
notes: Magiera is today's Mageira Street; Russell Av. is Russel Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Fit rests on seven control points (0.7 m RMSE) but gives 8.07 px per foot, about 2 percent above the atlas value.
The Northside Avenue junctions at the top were not detected and are not control points.
Spring is lettered with East in brackets on part of its length.
map, 50 ft, turned about +51. Division, Northside Av, Spring, Jeffrie Av, Whitehead Av, Yates Av, Magiera, Herman Av; cigar co.

sheet-18.description: Sheet 18 covers a dense district of frame dwellings in the southern part of South River, between Magiera at the top, Prentice Avenue at the bottom, Center Street at the left and Marion Street at the right. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned about 25 degrees, so that the long avenues run diagonally from upper left to lower right. Union Avenue, Southside Avenue and Prentice Avenue are crossed by Center Street, Bray Avenue, East Street and, at the lower edge, Pushkin and Tolstoy. Nearly every lot carries a dwelling with a rear outbuilding, a few stores and a laundry stand near East Street, a brick-coloured building near Union Avenue, and an embroidery works is shown at the top beside Spring. A building labelled Cinder Bl. stands on Prentice Avenue near Henry. Many lots at the left are still vacant or only outlined. Property lines are drawn finely, with lot numbers beside the frontages, and four-inch water pipes run in most streets. At the right edge, Marion runs diagonally past a block of houses to Prentice Avenue. The sheet adjoins sheets 16, 17, 20 and 27, and the compass at the upper right shows north tilted to the right of the page top.
notes: Magiera is today's Mageira Street; the other streets keep their printed names in OpenStreetMap, except that Henry is Henry Street.
Ten control points, RMSE 1.1 m, leave-one-out 1.6 m.
map, 50 ft. Magiera, Spring, Union Av, Center, Southside, Prentice Av, Bray Av, East, Marion, Pushkin, Tolstoy.

sheet-19.description: Sheet 19 shows the industrial strip along the Raritan River Railroad on the east side of South River, from the foot of Herman Avenue down to the brick works at the south. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper right. At the top left, Herman Avenue and Water run past rows of small frame dwellings. The South River Spinning Co., spinners and weavers of silk, fills the upper centre with a multi-storey pink factory and long sheds with raised skylights, a rolling department, an engine room and power plant, with a reservoir fed by a brook beside it. Below the factory the sheet is crossed by a broad railroad yard, with the passenger depot, a concrete platform, the freight depot and many curving running tracks. The lower half belongs to the American Enameled Brick & Tile Co., with clay sheds, a machine shop, pressing and drying rooms, steam-vent drying kilns, a bank of circular kilns, kiln sheds and a long storage shed for brick, bordered on the east by salt meadow; a wood trestle and a spur follow the plant's western side. Whitehead Avenue runs down the left edge, with Yates Avenue and Magiera crossing it and Serviss branching off to the southeast; a Raritan River R. R. hotel, wagon house and stores stand on the west side. A note block lists the watchman, power and fire protection of the brick works.
notes: Magiera is today's Mageira Street; Herman Av. is today's Herman Street.
Low confidence: placed by a helmert from four points all along Whitehead Avenue (three streets and one rail crossing); rotation and scale are only weakly controlled.
The Whitehead Avenue / Yates Avenue and Herman / Water junctions were not detected.

map, 50 ft. Works along the railroad and river: R. R. R. depot, spinning co., American Enameled Brick & Tile; Herman Av, Water, Whitehead Av, Yates Av, Serviss. Control only along Whitehead (helmert).

sheet-20.description: Sheet 20 covers the southeast part of South River, centred on Whitehead Avenue and Jeffrie Avenue. It is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points toward the upper right, which sets Whitehead Avenue nearly vertical. At the top, Magiera crosses Jeffrie Avenue and Whitehead Avenue, and Serviss runs southeast from Whitehead Avenue past a funeral home and a Russian bath house. Between the two avenues, blocks of frame dwellings and embroidery works line Jeffrie Avenue; an embroidery factory and an embroidery shop appear along its east side, and the Adam Schack Embroidery Factory stands on Prentice Avenue. In the middle, the Russian Catholic Church with its rectory and chapel occupies a block between Linden Avenue and Prentice Avenue. East of Whitehead Avenue, Levinson Avenue and Armstrong Avenue run southeast with long rows of narrow dwelling lots reaching to the edge of the sheet. At the upper right the yellow-coloured mass of the brick works' storage shed is cut by a railroad switch, and a small pond lies to the south of it. Marion and Tolstoy, Olchaskey Avenue and Schak Avenue are lettered at the left. Four-inch and six-inch water pipes are marked in nearly every street, and adjoining sheets 17, 18, 19 and 27 are cited.
notes: Magiera is today's Mageira Street; Olchaskey Av. is Olchasky Avenue; Schak Avenue is Schack Avenue; Serviss is Serviss Street at Whitehead Avenue.
Armstrong Avenue meets Whitehead Avenue at a modern junction about 50 m from the drawn one; that junction is left out.
Fit gives 7.56 px per foot, about 5 percent below the atlas value, with 0.9 to 2.4 m residuals; the sheet may be drawn slightly small.
map, 50 ft, turned about +46; fits about 4.5 percent small. Magiera, Jeffrie Av, Whitehead Av, Serviss, Linden Av, Prentice Av, Levinson Av, Armstrong Av.

sheet-21.description: Sheet 21 covers the south-western edge of South River and the adjoining part of East Brunswick Township, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north pointing up and slightly to the right. Devoe Avenue runs across the top of the sheet with Albourne, Beryl and Colfax (Glen) running up into the sheet 10 blocks above it. The Old Bridge-New Brunswick Turnpike crosses the sheet diagonally from the upper left to the lower right, carrying the borough limit between South River and East Brunswick Township and a six-inch water pipe. A railroad embankment with a concrete bridge crosses the turnpike north of Elm Street and continues to the right edge toward sheet 22. East of the turnpike the blocks between Devoe Avenue, Beryl and Colfax hold frame dwellings and an embroidery factory, and the Allgair (Center) and Palm Place frontages down to Hillside Avenue hold dwellings and a few brick and tile buildings. West of the turnpike, in East Brunswick Township, Elm Street (marked not opened), Park Place and Milltown Road cross the sheet in broad, mostly vacant blocks; the Wade School and a manufacturing concrete blocks building, an auto repair garage and a few dwellings are the main buildings. Water pipes of four and six inches follow most streets, and hydrants are marked at several corners. The lower right corner carries the scale bar and library stamp. Sheets 10, 22 and 24 adjoin this sheet.
notes: Devoe Avenue is Devoe Street today; Old Bridge-New Brunswick Turnpike is Old Bridge Turnpike; Milltown Road, Park Place, Elm, Hillside Avenue and Palm Place keep their names (Elm Street, Hillside Avenue).
Allgair is lettered with Center in brackets as an alternative name; Allgair Street today.
Elm is lettered Not Opened.
Names were read from the 1600 px overview, not full-resolution crops.
map, 50 ft. South-west edge: Devoe Av, Albourne, Beryl, Colfax, Old Bridge-New Brunswick Tpke, Elm, Park Pl, Milltown Road; East Brunswick west of the turnpike.

sheet-22.description: Sheet 22 covers the centre of the western part of South River, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north pointing up and slightly to the right. Devoe Avenue runs across the top with Colfax (Glen), Darrow, Wilcox Place and West George Street meeting it from the north. Main Street crosses the sheet diagonally from the lower left toward the upper right, and Pierson Street and Roosevelt run off it on the east side. Hillside Avenue forms the bottom edge, with Allgair, Clark, James and Albert crossing it, and Palm Place and Exton run down at the lower left. A railroad cuts across the sheet from the left edge to the lower right, with a wide right of way marked as block 116. The blocks along Main Street carry frame dwellings with a brick and tile works and a concrete block building near the railroad; the area between Devoe Avenue and the railroad has several brick and tile buildings drawn in red and pink, on Wilcox Place and Devoe Avenue frontages. South of the railroad the Hillside Avenue lots are narrow and sparsely built with frame dwellings and a drug store at the Main Street corner. Water pipes of four, six and ten inches follow the streets, with hydrants at many corners and a fire alarm box at Hillside and Allgair. Sheets 10, 11, 21, 23, 24 and 25 adjoin.
notes: Devoe Avenue is Devoe Street today; Hillside Avenue, Main, Pierson, Roosevelt, Allgair, Clark, James, Albert and Exton are Hillside Avenue, Main Street, Pierson Street, Roosevelt Street, Allgair Street, Clark Street, James Street, Albert Street and Exton Street.
Colfax is lettered with Glen in brackets as an alternative name.
Names were read from the 1600 px overview, not full-resolution crops.
map, 50 ft. Main St centre, Devoe Av to Hillside Av, Pierson, Roosevelt, Allgair, Palm Pl; railroad.

sheet-23.description: Sheet 23 covers the eastern part of the Main Street district of South River, drawn at 50 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left. Main Street runs down the left edge of the sheet; Devoe, Pierson, Grove and Pottery Lane meet it from the east. Roosevelt and High, laid out as a pair of diagonal streets, run from the upper centre toward the lower left and meet near the centre of the sheet. The blocks, numbered 117 to 120, are lined with frame dwellings, with brick and tile buildings drawn in red along Main Street, a print shop on High, and a concrete block building near Roosevelt. At the lower right a railroad runs diagonally from the bottom of the sheet toward the upper right, and Hillside Avenue appears in the extreme lower right corner. The upper right of the sheet is undeveloped land, with the words Old Quarry lettered in it. Water pipes of four and ten inches run in Main, Pierson, Grove and Pottery Lane, and hydrants and a fire alarm box are marked. The lower margin carries the scale bar and the library stamp. Sheets 11, 13, 22 and 25 adjoin; the neighbouring sheet numbers appear in the margins.
notes: Main, Pierson, Roosevelt, High, Grove and Pottery Lane keep their names today (Main Street, Pierson Street, Roosevelt Street, High Street, Grove Street, Pottery Lane).
Control is thin and Main Street is only partly drawn on this sheet.
Names were read from the 1600 px overview, not full-resolution crops.
map, 50 ft, turned about -33. Main, Pierson, Roosevelt, High, Grove, Pottery Lane, Old Quarry; few junctions.

sheet-24.description: Sheet 24 covers the south-western edge of South River where it meets East Brunswick Township, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north pointing up and to the right. The Old Bridge-New Brunswick Turnpike runs down the middle of the sheet and carries the borough limit between South River and East Brunswick Township. Milltown Road crosses the upper left of the sheet and joins the turnpike, Hillside Avenue enters from the upper right, and Main Street, Cranbury Road, Wallace and McPherson cross it lower down. Willow runs down the left side and Exton and Clark down the right. East of the turnpike the blocks hold frame dwellings and some brick buildings, with a filling station near Main Street and a vacant tile building near McPherson; west of it in East Brunswick Township an auto repair building, a dairy, a bottle storage building and an embroidery works stand along the turnpike and Milltown Road, and block 74 holds a second embroidery building. Water pipes of four, six and ten inches follow the streets, and a stand pipe stands near Exton. Sheets 21, 22, 25 and 26 adjoin. The lower left corner carries the scale bar.
notes: Old Bridge-New Brunswick Turnpike is Old Bridge Turnpike today; Cranbury is Cranbury Road and McPherson is McPherson Place.
Names were read from the 1600 px overview, not full-resolution crops.
map, 50 ft, turned about +35. Old Bridge-New Brunswick Tpke, Milltown Road, Hillside Av, Main, Cranbury, Willow, Wallace, McPherson.

sheet-25.description: Sheet 25 covers a residential district in the south of South River, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north pointing up and to the right. Hillside Avenue forms the upper edge, running from the upper left to the right. Clark, James and Albert run from Hillside Avenue down the sheet, with David on the right, and Melrose Place, Johnson Place and Fairview Avenue cross them. The blocks, numbered 85 to 94, are lined with frame dwellings of two storeys with outbuildings; the Hillside Avenue frontage has an auto repair and garage building, an embroidery works and other commercial buildings drawn in blue and yellow. In the lower right the William Campbell School, a large brick building with a gymnasium and auditorium, stands on block 94. Water pipes of four and six inches follow the streets and hydrants are marked at many corners. Parts of the right side are open land. Sheets 22, 24, 26 and 13 adjoin along the edges, as the margin numbers show. The lower margin carries the scale bar and the library stamp.
notes: Hillside Avenue, Clark, James, Albert, David and Fairview Avenue are Hillside Avenue, Clark Street, James Street, Albert Street, David Street and Fairview Avenue today.
Names were read from the 1600 px overview, not full-resolution crops.
map, 50 ft, turned about +35. Hillside Av, Clark, James, Albert, David, Melrose Pl, Johnson Pl, Fairview Av; Campbell School.

sheet-26.description: Sheet 26 covers a residential district in the south-west of South River along the Old Bridge-New Brunswick Turnpike, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north pointing up and to the right. The turnpike runs down the middle of the sheet and carries the borough limit between South River and East Brunswick Township. East of it Johnson Place, Fairview Avenue, Arlington Avenue and Lexington Avenue run across the sheet from the turnpike to James, with Clark entering at the top. McPherson is at the top edge. West of the turnpike, in East Brunswick Township, Wallace, Fountain and Marietta cross the sheet with Willow down the left edge; the area is lettered East Brunswick Township. The blocks, numbered 78 to 102, are lined with frame dwellings, with an embroidery shop at the top left. The bottom of the sheet carries a note that the dwellings front on Claremont Av. Water pipes of four, six and eight inches follow the streets. Sheets 24, 25 and 13 adjoin. The scale bar is near the bottom.
notes: Old Bridge-New Brunswick Turnpike is Old Bridge Turnpike today; Wallace is Wallace Street, McPherson is McPherson Place, Fountain is Fountain Street and Marietta is Marietta Street.
Claremont Avenue is named in a note at the bottom of the sheet.
Names were read from the 1600 px overview, not full-resolution crops.
map, 50 ft, turned about +35. Wallace, McPherson, Johnson Pl, Fairview, Arlington, Lexington, Claremont Av, Fountain, Marietta; East Brunswick west of the turnpike.

sheet-27-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 27 is the main map of the sheet, drawn at 100 feet to an inch (half the scale of most of the atlas) and turned so that north points up and to the right. It covers the southern edge of South River around Whitehead Avenue, which runs down the middle of the part from Prentice and Armstrong Avenues past Robert and Augusta Streets towards the proposed Ann and Bank streets near the river. West of Whitehead Avenue lie Prentice, Olchaskey and Schak Avenues and Robert Street, with frame dwellings on narrow lots in blocks 179 to 181; east of it Levinson and Armstrong Avenues, Augusta Street and Kathryn Street run across the part, lined with one- and two-storey frame dwellings, a few stores and outbuildings, in blocks 171 to 174 and 183 to 184. Buildings of note are the Riverside Hotel and a summer pavilion near Whitehead Avenue and a shirt factory with individual motors on Robert Street. The lower half of the part is largely open ground (blocks 182, 184 to 186), crossed by a ten-inch water pipe running to the water works. Heavy lines separate this part from the insets of the sheet: the Hillside Avenue blocks at the upper right, the Paragon Brick and National Materials works at the left, the South River Electric and Gas plant at the right, and the Causeway along the South River at the bottom.
notes: Schak Avenue is Schack Avenue and Olchaskey Avenue is Olchasky Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Ann and Bank are lettered as proposed streets; Ann is probably today's Anne Street.
Drawn at 100 feet to an inch; the fitted scale is about 4 percent larger than the atlas's 50 ft sheets imply.
Armstrong Avenue is drawn meeting Whitehead Avenue opposite Prentice Avenue; the modern Armstrong Avenue junction lies about 50 m further north-west, so it was not used as control.

sheet-27-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 27 is an inset at the upper right of the sheet, outlined by a heavy line, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the left. It shows a block on the west side of South River near the East Brunswick line, beside sheets 24 to 26: Hillside Avenue runs down the right side of the inset, with Chestnut Street crossing it near the top and Teresa Place leaving it to the east near the bottom. Most of the inset, block 118, is occupied by a vacant plant, formerly the South River Chemical Works, with concrete-block and frame buildings; the lots of blocks 89 and 90 on Hillside Avenue and Teresa Place carry frame dwellings and an embroidery factory, and block 257 at the top holds a few dwellings on Chestnut Street. A six-inch water pipe runs in Hillside Avenue. The left and lower edges are marked no exposure.
notes: Chestnut on this inset is today's Ford Street (it meets Hillside Avenue about 170 m east of Theresa Place); the modern Chestnut Street is in the north of the borough.
Teresa Place is Theresa Place in OpenStreetMap.

sheet-27-5.description: Part 5 of sheet 27 is the strip along the bottom of the sheet, below a heavy dividing line, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with its own north arrow pointing up and to the right. It follows the Causeway, the road running east from Water Street at the upper left across the marshes on the south bank of the South River to the iron bridge at the lower right. Frame dwellings, a garage and auto repair shop and a few stores line the Causeway near Water Street (block 244); further east the street lettered Road leaves the Causeway to the south, with the short arbitrary street Fern and a small group of dwellings beside it, and a tinsmith shop, a feed store and cement storage stand on the Causeway. The Public Service Corporation sub-power station stands north of the Causeway in block 144. The South River winds across the part north of the Causeway and again along the bottom, with marsh on both sides. A four-inch water pipe runs in the Causeway. The scale bar is at the lower right.
notes: The street lettered Road is today's Browns Lane.
Fern is marked as an arbitrary name.

sheet-28.description: Sheet 28 shows Washington Heights, a residential development in East Brunswick Township on the north-western edge of South River, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north at the top. Six parallel streets cross the sheet from left to right: Prospect along the top edge, then Wilmot, Amherst, Highland, Parker and Aldrich along the bottom edge; Pine runs down the middle of the sheet, and the Old Bridge-New Brunswick Turnpike runs diagonally down the right side, with the boundary between East Brunswick Township and the Borough of South River marked along it. The blocks, numbered 213 to 223 and 225, are divided into regular narrow house lots, each with its lot number, and are still very thinly built: scattered one- and two-storey frame dwellings with small outbuildings, a few brick buildings near Prospect and the turnpike, and one stone or concrete-block building near Highland. Most lots are vacant. The open triangle east of the turnpike (block 225) belongs to South River. The title panel at the upper right reads Washington Heights, East Brunswick Township; the scale bar is at the lower right.
notes: Pine is today's Modzelewski Street; Prospect and Amherst are West Prospect Street and West Amherst Street west of the turnpike; Highland is Highland Street.
The Prospect Street junction with the turnpike was detected on the wrong line and excluded.
